steps.notes: SpeciesGrowth(g,pref,Rs,alive); 1-based resource indices stated explicitly in prompt; my impl passes all 3 tests in joint mode.
OneCycle: transcendental depletion times via root_scalar, yield=1 conversion given by background ODEs; passes all 3 tests incl. short-T partial-depletion case.

SimulatedCycles over N_cycles=1000; robust impl returns correct survivor lists [0,1,2]/[1,2]/[0,1,2,3] in <0.4s/test. Naive subtract-and-threshold impl can run away (see assessment) but a faithful impl that zeros the first-depleted resource is fast.

overall_assessment: Problem 26 (CRM_in_serial_dilution) is fair to score as-is. Dependencies import cleanly (numpy 2.2.6 / scipy 1.15.2). All three function headers match their test-case call signatures (D1 clear). The spec is complete: resource preference indexing is explicitly 1-based ('resources are indexed from 1 to R'), the 1:1 resource->biomass conversion and exponential-growth ODEs are given in the 26.2 background, and there is no randomness or timing dependence (deterministic; np.argsort tie-breaking in 26.3 test 2 is stable and matches the target's construction). h5 targets are well-formed (26.1 growth+resource arrays, 26.2 species+resource arrays, 26.3 integer survivor lists) and adequately constraining: no single trivial constant survivor list passes all three 26.3 cases. A clean literal-reading implementation passes all 3 steps under the official joint harness. Note (not a data defect): the obvious 'subtract consumed amount, zero resources below 1e-12' implementation hits a floating-point runaway in the OneCycle inner loop around cycle 37 of 26.3 test 2 (a resource left at ~1.4e-12 just above the threshold causes a near-infinite niche loop), which would exceed the 1800s timeout. This is implementation fragility, not a defect in the (prompt, test_cases, target) triple: the prompt explicitly instructs to compute the state 'at the time of that depletion', so a faithful implementation that sets the first-depleted resource exactly to 0 (as my robust version does) completes each test in well under a second and matches the targets.
